title: The most common word
starter:
def most_common(words: list[str]) -> tuple[str, int] | None:
    return (words[0], 1)
hints: First count the words into a dict, as in the counting example above.
Then sort `counts.items()` with a key that returns `(-count, word)`. The biggest count comes first, and ties go alphabetically. Take element `[0]`.
An empty list has no most common word. Check for it first and return `None`.

answer.explain: The reference counts with a dict, then sorts the `(word, count)` pairs by `(-count, word)` and takes the first. Negating the count puts the biggest first while the word still sorts A to Z, so ties go to the alphabetically first word. An empty list returns `None`.
